decisions.reason: The infinite affine refinement counterexample is valid. The false last sentence is unused: quasi-compactness gives the finite subcover in 1.1; effective algebra descent and morphism descent identify X_U with Spec D, and faithful flat module descent proves finiteness. Replaced only that ancillary sentence; the Statement is unchanged.

The counterexample shows why finite type matters to the display title. The Statement already includes it, and step 2.1 uses finite algebra generators. Finite coefficient contractions give directed finite subcomodules; counit extraction shows matrix coefficients generate k[G], so the representation is a closed immersion even for nonreduced G. Qualified only the title; Statement and proof are unchanged.

F1 attributed existence of a Galois closure and the embedding count to an interface that states neither. Repaired with existing primitive-element, splitting-field existence and finite algebraic-generation suppliers: L=k(alpha), its separable degree-n minimal polynomial has a finite Galois splitting field, and evaluation at its n distinct roots gives all embeddings. The commutative sum of torsor trivializations is Galois invariant and descends, with no division by n. Statement unchanged.

The field-tests interface gives geometric-regularity descent, not smoothness equivalence. Added the smooth-morphism definition and Jacobian criterion, explicitly bridging local standard smoothness and checking finite presentation, k-flatness and geometrically regular fibres. The high-power image argument and finite-kernel calculation remain sound; Statement unchanged.

The cited jet theorem assumes scheme faithfulness, which conjugation need not satisfy. Replaced that unlicensed invocation with a direct construction and Noetherian stabilization, then coefficientwise Krull intersection and schematic density after arbitrary base change to identify the stable kernel with the centre. Nonreduced kernel parameters are retained. Statement unchanged.

The disconnected-group counterexample refutes the unrestricted title, while the Statement already requires smooth geometric integrality. Its defect map extends over the smooth anti-affine completion factor and rigidity kills it; faithful scalar extension descends the multiplication identity. Qualified the title and matching page prose, and corrected the contract claim about identity preservation by homomorphisms. Statement and proof unchanged.

The cited algebra theorem only composes locally standard smooth maps; F3 supplied no bridge from the fibre definition. Replaced it by the published scheme theorem using that definition. Specified fibres over algebraic closures of residue fields and geometric-regularity descent, with explicit closure and rational-point suppliers. The torsor kernel pair proves affine transfer, faithful pullback proves geometric reducedness of Q, and open connected fibres prove connected transfer. Statement unchanged.

before_statements.lem-nonaffine-affine-and-finite-morphism: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $p:S'\to S$ be faithfully flat, quasi-compact, and locally of finite presentation, and $f:X\to S$ a finite-type separated morphism of Noetherian schemes. If $X_{S'}\to S'$ is affine, then $f$ is affine. If that base change is finite, then $f$ is finite.
before_statements.lem-nonaffine-affine-group-faithful-repr: Let $G$ be an affine finite-type group scheme over an arbitrary field $k$. Every right comodule over its coordinate Hopf algebra $A=k[G]$ is the filtered union of its finite-dimensional subcomodules. The right regular representation of $G$ on $A$ contains a finite-dimensional subrepresentation $V$ such that $G\to\operatorname{GL}(V)$ is a closed immersion. These assertions allow nonreduced $G$.
before_statements.lem-nonaffine-commutative-torsor-norm-ma:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $G$ be a commutative separated finite-type $k$-group scheme and let $V$ be a $G$-torsor over $k$. Here a torsor means a faithfully flat finite-presentation $k$-scheme with an action written $v+g$ for which $(v,g)\mapsto(v,v+g)$ is an isomorphism $V\times_kG\cong V\times_kV$. Suppose that $V$ has a point $P$ with finite separable residue field $L/k$ of degree $n$. Then there is a $k$-morphism $\phi:V\to G$ with
$$\phi(v+g)=\phi(v)+ng$$
as an identity of morphisms $V\times_kG\to G$. If $V$ is smooth and nonempty, such a point $P$ exists.
before_statements.lem-nonaffine-high-frobenius-smooth-imag: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $G$ be a separated finite-type group scheme over a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$. For $n\ge1$ put $G^{(n)}=G\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k,F_k^n}\operatorname{Spec}k$. The relative Frobenius $F^n_{G/k}:G\to G^{(n)}$ is finite and is a group homomorphism. For sufficiently large $n$, its scheme-theoretic image $H_n\subset G^{(n)}$ is a smooth finite-type group scheme. If $G$ is connected then $H_n$ is connected. The kernel of $G\to H_n$ is finite. This does not assert that the whole twist $G^{(n)}$ becomes smooth.
before_statements.lem-nonaffine-centre-is-stable-jet-kerne: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $G$ be a smooth geometrically integral finite-type group scheme over $k$. Conjugation gives representations on $\mathcal O_{G,e}/\mathfrak m_e^{n+1}$. Their kernels stabilize for large $n$, and the stable kernel is the scheme-theoretic centre $Z(G)$.
before_statements.thm-nonaffine-pointed-group-to-abelian-v: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $G$ be a smooth geometrically integral group variety over a field $k$, and $A$ an abelian variety. Every $k$-morphism $f:G\to A$ with $f(e_G)=e_A$ is a group homomorphism.
